I bought NMS in 2016 and I was sorely disappointed as the game was empty and buggy: it felt more like an untested alpha version than a polished game. I managed to get a refund after playing for seven hours (!) through Steam and I decided I would never touch anything that Hello Games would make again. Fast forward to 2020: as I read more positive reviews and saw quite a few videos I became interested again. I went ahead and bought the game again: I have no regrets this time :-)

The game can be finished in about 10 hours if you just focus on one goal: so why did I spend 100+ hours there? Well think of Skyrim or Morrowind: there is the prime narrative that you can complete but there is so much other things to do: call it exploring :-) And then again it's open ended the primary goal is just one thing you can achieve but there is much more to do. 

While the graphics aren't of the serious level like Elite Dangerous or Star Citizen it doesn't mean this is a game you should ignore if you are interested in space exploration or building. It is impressive to see all the elements that Hello Games have added and not charging any DLC for it. There is so much to do: building a Star Destroyer fleet, farming, mining, learning alien languages or become a superhero with near unlimited powers. Special mention is for the base building: together with the ability to change the landscape pretty much how you want it, it means you can build an underground ice base or an outpost on a desert world or anything in between. It's quite an enjoyable aspect of the game (*note: after being a large underground base I found that there are limitations in the game and the terrain will be reset after a while - to prevent disappointments I recommend to build all bases on frames and to not alter the terrain at your base at all).

The mission design for the different factions is just rinse and repeat: similar to Elite Dangerous but it becomes better if you go to the multiplayer hub where there are more interesting missions offered. I was very impressed doing a mission, flying to a planet and meeting other players. It's great to see that you can meet PC and console players: so no more wars between who is best we all enjoy the same game :-) 

In one mission a few players were in trouble because a giant mech was chasing them; I just helped them and my Exotic ship made quick work of the mech. There are a few larger story arc missions that in general are quite well written; it provides with a lot of lore and I was surprised to see that it even answered a few questions I had like why do the drones just suddenly appear (I thought it was just a limitation of the game). 

Of course, the best aspect is to explore and see new worlds. The art style is much improved so you won't see deadly potatoes flying through the sky anymore; I quite like it. And there are crashed ships, lost temples, seas and caves to explore. Perhaps you will meet a NPC that needs help in deep space or you find a glitched world with some impressive designs (think Dr Who or one of the special ST:TNG episodes). The recent addition of exploring derelict freighters brings a completely new experience and hopefully we will see more of those in future.  Special mention is for the sound: this is done very well! 

Perhaps the negative things are still some bugs - not game breaking but noticeable. One thing that really annoyed me is what I mentioned before: the limit on the amount of editing you can do on a map. I had perhaps three times during a 100-hour play sessions that the game would crash to windows. I didn't lose too much progress but of course this shouldn't happen anymore. The other slight issue I have is that certain progress is quite grindy: not GW2 grindy but more than single player games offer. However, there is so much to do that it didn't bother me so much. 

Having played Elite Dangerous and Star Citizen I would have preferred a more challenging flight model as it feels more like flying on a console than any of those games. It would definitely improve the game a lot. I played on standard difficulty and the enemies didn't give any challenge to me after I upgraded at the beginning of the game. It would be nice to have super dangerous enemies lurking around. 

All in all though if you are interested in SciFi and you can get this game on sale I recommend it. It will give you an experience you won't find in many other games.

Some advice/ minor spoilers: the game doesn't force you to do anything most of the time. So when I finally decided to complete the initial quests many things that the quest were trying to teach me I already knew: I had assembled a freighter with 25 frigates, 400M in credit and 11K in nanites and 5K quicksilver with a fully upgraded ship, suit and roamer. It felt a bit silly that I then had to chase some quest to get a 100 nanites but I understand why this is put in place. At least it did give me some blueprints that I was desperate for :-). Looking back, I probably should have started with the quests first. At the very least I would advise to advance to the point that you have access to the anomaly.

Original Review:
It strikes me, reading through most reviews, that a lot of people were expecting a rather ridiculous range of things from this little indie game; so in lieu of a traditional review, i think instead I'll simply tell you what No Man's Sky is, and what it isn't.

What it is ...

- Art
- Inventory management sim
- Survival genre hybrid
- Technologically impressive
- Exploration heavy
- Oddly relaxing

What it isn't ...

- Multiplayer
- A new religion
- Better than sex
- Elite: Dangerous
- Star Citizen
- Endless grinding (just for a bit, in the beginning)

The more I play, the more I enjoy, and I couldn't recommend this game enough, but I knew what it'd be going in. A lot of people climbed onto the hype train and they aren't getting off anytime soon, and their reviews are all here if you're wondering how they feel. But for what it's worth ...

- If you loved the exploration of the first Mass Effect
- If your best memory of Kerbal Space Program is stepping foot on another planet
- If Minecraft is or ever was something you enjoyed playing
- If your inner child hasn't been smothered to death by the crushing indifference of everyday life
- If your inner child is dead, but you've got a few hrs to burn anyway ...

... You will probably love No Man's Sky.

**Edit 2 as of 7/26/2020**
Felt like playing a space game, and figured I would give this game a go again from the start.

**Edit**
The game has updated... and released new content.
Generally speaking, if you enjoy the style of game, this is now a viable entry to your library.
The concept of a completable story/content is still more open-ended, but the game itself has improved in all the right places to now be recommended.

See the review below for the old review and a lot of the problems from before.


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If you are on the fence, jump off and spend your money elsewhere. 

I read the reviews, saw some footage, and I thought--Oh. It cant be that bad. 

After about 4 hours, there was NOTHING NEW to do. It was a grind fest.

If you are into exploring and looking at randomly generated structures and animals, then you may survive this game.

But if you are looking for any hard-core goal-oriented gameplay, keep looking.


This game lingers tiny bits of backstory that you think may provide some ultimate storyline, that leads to an ultimate end. 2 different choices (going with atlas, or chosing your own path).--Both of which are severely disappointing. Atlas simply requires that you grind, and get rewarded for your grinding, until even the game says you've done enough grinding, and then it says "congratulations--now a star is born" or something equally as disappointing.  

And the center of the universe? Try a huge "New Game+" button. No story, no explanation, no rewards... no cross-cultural explanation or society, no satisfaction whatsoever besides the experience of exploration.


And for a game that can ONLY offer the experience of RNG exploration, you get your decent fill after about 2-4 hours.

I personally try to use a scale for games. I want to have 'fresh' content/experience at a ratio of $1/hr. Indie games, i will give a higher rating to if they warrant it (eg $2-3/hr). This game is demanding a whopping $15/hr of enjoyment, and if you want to get your $/hr value, you just need to grind.
This game deserves a $20 pricetag. MAYBE a launch tag of $30. But until there is some sort of actual content that shows some intention to provide designed quality outside of a RNG atmosphere, this game is a no-go.



Long story short-- If you are looking for something fresh, exciting, and completable, keep looking--especially at a cheaper price point.

This game may not be for everyone. I personally really enjoy it but I liken it to Metroid. Its an experience in isolation, exploration and discovery. Update 19/7/2020 - Desolation update. This game has come a long way since my previous review and while it still is not perfect there's a lot more to this game now. The game still has major bugs, so be warned of that prior to playing. There is so much to do in this game now it is a bit overwhelming, but in a great way. They've made it so that there is multiplayer across platforms, but its not necessary to engage with if you don't want to. There is drop-in multiplayer, a hub location to setup missions with other players, and you can even just invite friends into your game so they can warp directly to your system and play with you on the fly.

Ships are better now in their control schemes, as well as being fully upgradeable. No customisation options but there are enough ship types with different color combinations to almost make up for this. Freighters can be bought, upgraded, and customised. You can own a fleet of frigates to accompany your capital ship and send them out on missions to make serious money. Freighters and frigates do not participate in space battles and there's no fleet vs. fleet mechanic. There may be in the future and I hope it is added.

There are so many, SO MANY things to do and discover that it is mind-blowing. Derelict freighters with their crews missing or dead that you can search for loot in a horror style gameplay mixup with no life support systems or artificial gravity. Body parts strewn about floating through the ship as you hunt creatures in the darkness and uncover the mystery of what happened to the ship's crew. Passing starships who will raise your comms to ask for assistance or just offer to trade rare items. Mysterious interstellar beings that float through space waiting to be discovered. Ridiculous amount of planet types, upgrades for tools, base building components, quests, terrain alteration, and so much more. 

It still may not be for everyone but I still support Sean Murray and Hello Games for the crazy amount of dedication they've put into this and are still delivering.

***UPDATE 15 SEP 2020***

So, I put this game to bed for a while, as it had far too many bugs and was very empty - to the point of boredom.  However with several large updates, and many smaller fixes - this is now a far closer experience to the original promised at launch.

I won't forget what Hello Games did - quite literally they were writing cheques that the game couldn’t cash.  However, rather than just abandon the game, they have stuck with it.  I hope they have learnt a valuable lesson, and frankly I think there are many other developers that could learn and important lesson from them too.

Not everything is rosy though, some textures still take an age to load in.  Once you’ve got a decent upgrade or two for your jetpack you will see that all of the grass (and often the rocks and crates) vanish...only to appear out of thin air.  It is at it’s worst when you are moving fast – but can happen just be looking around.

Quite often, if you use the terrain modifier, it leaves hidden walls behind...not ideal when you are trying to make a quick fox hole to escape a storm.

But for the most part this game is now good.  The new content is a joy, I just spent a week getting myself a living ship.  The new encounters add some variety, and we have multiplayer and cross platform play!

I think there is still more for them to do...but I can happily give this game a thumbs up now!

***UPDATE 17 SEP 2016***

So, after a few patches and no correspondence from the developers I have changed my mind about this game - even more so the developer "Hello Games".  A patch that was released killed the game for me, it just crashed on start (not even getting past the Havok logo).  I logged a support ticket and finally got a response after two (2) weeks!  It was a generic, cookie cutter, response that only stated they had released a patch.  Very poor customer support.

Performance has gotten worse, stuttering/hitching is now beyond a joke and we have all learnt that there is NO "end game" revelation.  I really hope that Hello Games does include the features they have said they would, but I no longer have any confidence that they will.

This game has so much potential, but now I don't think it will ever live up to it.

***UPDATE COMPLETE***

I have been looking forward to this game for quite some time, but does it live up to the hype?

Well, yes and no - at the end of the day if you like flying around (almost aimlessly) looking for mineral X or animal Y or vegetable Z then this game is very good.  If you don't, move along home.

I feel I am one of the lucky ones, I don't have any major performance issues (max settings @ 1920*1200 45-59 FPS) - but that is not to say things are perfect. In order to keep this brief I'll sum this up below:

[b][i]The good[/i][/b]:

[list]
    [*]Going to get my moneys worth out of this
    [*]Very pretty for the most part
    [*]Gorgeous audio design
    [*]Interesting exploration
    [*]Scary as hell (for example - when you realise your 5 minutes from shelter with 4 1/2 minutes of protection)
    [*]Developer seems to have an eye on the future (bases, freighters) - time will tell if this pans out.
[/list]

[b][i]The bad[/i][/b]:

[list]
    [*]Micro stutters for no apparent reason, probably related to the shader cache issue.
    [*]Very limited "help" from the game to teach you how to play the game.
    [*]Controls (keyboard/mouse) when walking are fine (exception below), flight controls are another story.
    [*]"Sprint" turns off the instant your feet leave the ground. VERY frustrating when your running down a stepped incline.
    [*]Apparently no way to auto refill shields/engines/weapons - NOT great when you are in combat!
    [*]Galactic map navigation is VERY poor. Unable to find previous systems and "find discoveries" doesn't seem to do anything - server related?
    [*]Textures are often low quality.
    [*]Several star systems had exactly the same flaura and fauna? Should I expect to see Chestnut trees on Mars and Europa?
[/list]

[b][i]The ugly[/i][/b]:

[list]
    [*]Alt-Tab = crash
    [*]Flickering textures on space stations - fixed by disabling steam overlay, but this is a workaround not a fix.
    [*]Getting random CTD every now and then, no pattern, no obvious cause, and it's not often.
[/list]

Would I recommend? Yes, but with a hint of caution. If your expecting a flawless experience (which NO game can provide) you might be disappointed, there are some rough edges and I get the impression that the 1.03 patch was rushed for a day zero completion time - Hello Games should learn a valuable lesson here, delay is ALWAYS better than rush.

-------------------------------------Below is Launch Review---------------------------------------------------------------------

I was mildly excited for this game to come out.  The idea of exploring a seemingly infinite universe sounds awesome.  And discovering and naming animals/planets seemed like it would be a cool little feature to include.  

However, this game was not at all worth the hype it recieved.  Don't get me wrong, I have about 13 hours clocked on this game and for the most part it's been fun, but it gets repetitive very fast.

When I firsted started the game, it was really exciting.  New game.  New world.  Since I didn't watch many gameplay videos, it felt like there was an infinite possibilities to the game.  The graphics to the game were really good, too. The first planet is the most fun, in my opinion.  Everything you do on that planet is a first.  You find your first creature to document, you find your first plants.  You mine resources and you repair a spaceship.  However, it soon becomes apparent that that's pretty much it to the game.  I mean, there are special locations where you can find aliens, but they're nothing more than a one encounter event usually only offering blueprints that you can find elsewhere.  

So the game is pretty much just travelling to planets, (you can document stuff to earn money, but it's not necessary), mining resources, possibly upgrading your tools, mining resources, maybe getting a new ship, and mining resources.  You need resources for fuels and whenever you're on a planet, your exosuit is taking some sort of damage so you need to keep on fixing it.  And replenishing your mining tool from.... mining.  Oh, and trying to manage your inventory since you start with so little space.  

While the idea of 18 quintillion planets seems impressive, it's really not.  The planets really aren't that interesting even if they have different sizes, colors, plantlife, animals.  The animals just feel like you're watching a SPORE game and everything else is just some form of mineral to mine.

So, I found out that all of the player data is stored client side and can be edited, not only to give yourself everything, including editing every item seed, but you can give yourself stuff that the game never intended. You can edit your ship and multitool to be able to one-shot other players that haven't turned off PvP damage, while you take almost no damage at all.
You can also give yourself all off  the currency, including quicksilver, tho that doesn't matter either, because you can simply unlock everything (emotes, decor, jetpack and starship trails, everything). You can give yourself more storage space than you can normally get by grinding and maxing out all of your stuff.

Once I found all of this out, the game became so utterly boring, that after a billion years of playing, I had to uninstall it. That and every planet has the exact same assets: icy planets all have the same looking plants, every planet of the same type have the exact same assets as all the others of the same type. It's so extremely rare to find something cool looking that it's not even worth it.

Then you get to the center of a galaxy or two and move on to the next galaxy, where everything looks exactly the same, except for the color of the center of the galaxy, and the difficulty is raised slightly.

Reviews.214294:
I wrote this review at release, and so I am updating the review as the game is so much more expansive and so much been added since. 

The biggest thing to take away from this game, is that it is pretty much the ultimate universe sandbox you can find. "The universe of No Man's Sky comprises 255 unique galaxies. In turn, these are comprised of: 3 to 4 billion regions. each of which contain more than 122 and up to roughly 550 star systems." 

Let that sink in for just a moment.. 

While the artistic nature itself is more cartoony and light hearted, if you're alright with that, the game offers more than any other space exploration game out there by far. 
--------------------------------------

It's also very important to note, that Sean has kept all his promises to this date.. Constant free updates, everything promised has been added as he said they would. (Take that naysayers)

With the latest one adding procedurally generated "dungeons" inside of destroyed freighters, while you crawl around inside it and find out what went wrong. Each one being procedurally generated and never the same as before. 

While Multiplayer exists, you can turn it off if you want a pure Single Player game, but are allowed to open it up with just friends if you want, or dynamically shift between multiplayer and single player on the fly. 

There are also 100's of exceptional mods for the game, which expand it in many ways that you can find. From more base building parts, planet generation mods, animal and creature mods, color pallete mods, etc. 

-------------------------------------

Gameplay: 

The gameplay is very much explore, and explore more, while gathering resources, and learning new ways to survive better. 

You'll go from a crashed lonely explorer trying to repair your small ship, to owning a fleet of large capital ships with multiple bases, mining bases, and a host of personal ships ranging from combat ships, alien ships, and cargo ships. 

The base building is quite exceptional as well, as you can build.. literally anywhere. I have built an underground base via a series of tunnels I found, with another connecting tunnel that exits underwater for a submarine base, I then built an underground parking ramp complete with automated doors for my vehicles. The Orange/blue glow of the plants gives off an eerie yet peaceful decor. 

If base building isn't your thing, you can also use your capital ship you can get as your moveable base. Which you can warp around with, and build an interior inside of complete with everything a planetary base could have. From this Freighter, you can send your other ships out on missions. 

While your ships are away doing their thing, you can gain reputation (or lose reputation if you want to be a pirate), with the 3 main factions of the game, while taking missions, or attacking their freighters and stealing the goods. 

----------------------------------------

This game is an exceptional piece of art, and there seems to be many more updates planned in the future.

i5 3570k 4.0ghz - 16gb RAM - GTX 970

Searching for little outposts seems cool at first until you realize every single one is basically the same outpost and really only serves the purpose of being a waypoint on the map and a place where you might be able to learn a new word in some made up language.

Overall the game is uninspiring and rather bland. The game has potential if the quirks get worked out, and some people will love the game for what it is. I won't be commenting on the "multiplayer" as I think that's pretty obvious so far.

[h1][b]Updated Review[/b][/h1]

This is, by far, NOT the same game it was when it launched. While it is certainly still irritating that Sean Murray and HG decided to lie about their product at launch, I have to say that they have COMPLETELY changed my opinion about this game. 

This. is. the. game. I. pre-ordered. 100%. 

This game has so many things to offer and most of the content within the game has been implemented so well. 

Yes, there is still the annoying UI that comes up when you get an achievement, but you can now skip it. 

No longer does your ship hover at 12,000 ft in the air - you can smack into the ground now, and you'll take damage! 

The planets are absolutely gorgeous, the base building has been MOSTLY implemented extremely well, and the random generation is the best I've ever seen in a game, ever. 

They do need to fix the bases, though, because currently, if you flatten an area to build a base, at some point, the game will regenerate the terrain and bury your base, forcing you to mine it out all over again. I think this is probably the biggest complaint I have. 

They could fix that by preventing terrain generation within a certain radius around a base computer. If you wanted to then move your base, you could take your base comp and move it elsewhere, and that region would then regenerate at a later time. 

Do I recommend this game at $60? You bet your ass I do. This game is definitely worth $60. 

I will leave my original review here so you can see the transformation of this game. 



[h1][b]Original Review[/b][/h1]
I'm giving this game a recommendation to buy, but not at $60. The game was sold to us as something completely different than what it is. It's an "artsy fartsy" kind of game with surprisingly little content. It is fun - for what it is - but this game is by no means worthy of a AAA price. It is buggy, repetitive, and too much like an Early Access game for the price. 

If you see this game for half off, then get it because it's worth $30.00 to me, but because they lied to a lot of people, hyped it into a frenzy that was unwarranted, and gave us an incomplete game, I'd say wait until it's $5 to teach them a good lesson - stop lying. 


[b]Takes too long[/b]:
[list]


[*][i]Achievements:[/i]
Everytime you gain an achievement (of which there are many), your screen will be brought into 'cinematic mode' (black bar top/bottom) and you'll lose the ability to interact with anything for 20-60 seconds until it goes away. During that time, huge wording spreads across what little portion of the screen you have left (and I'm using a 41-inch monitor to play on). 

[*][i]Scanning:[/i]
In order to find new points-of-interest, you'll have to use these little beacons. But before you can choose from either Monolith, Colonial Outpost, Transmission, or Shelter, you'll wait 8-10 seconds for it to pull up this pretty-UI and then the game types out the words (the same basic words). Then you can choose from the aforementioned list of things, then wait another 15-20 seconds for it to 'scan' and find something. 

It's clear that it was meant to be "pretty" and "cool." It was pretty and cool the first time, but not the second, and most certainly not the 100th. These things need to happen immediately (or give players an option to turn that off). 

[*][i]Conversation:[/i]
In the game, you'll come across intelligent life and they can give you BPs, isotopes, oxides, etc. But before you can do that, you have to interact with them and play a stupid mini-game that still seems totally random (the answer is random, it seems). 

Before you even get to that point, the same UI that is used for everything else pops up and you have to wait ~30-40 seconds for the alien-guy to type out the text, then to populate a little 'mini-story', and THEN you get the option to do something. The whole process takes over a minute each time, and you will come across this VERY often, which amounts to it being excruciatingly annoying. 

[*][i]Everything:[/i]
Just about everything other than the 'world' stuff simply takes too long to finish. The same bland UI is used and the attempt to make it look "cool" or maybe even "artsy" means you have to wait forever and a day to do ANYTHING in the game. 

Want to trade with a space station? Sure, but you're going to wait 5-10 seconds just to get to where you hold-click on "sell or buy." It may not seem like a lot of time, but trust me - when you have to deal with this every. single. interaction with anything. . . it becomes annoying. 


[*][i]Walking:[/i]
Walking in this game is nothing short of hair-pulling nonsense. It is slow and frustrating. 

[*][i]JetPacking:[/i]
So you have a Jetpack, right? Wrong. You have a 22-inch boxfan strapped to your back, because that's about the same amount of get-up your pack has. Are there upgrades? Maybe, but since you have to place all upgrades in your inventory, it's unlikely you'll be packing around much in the way of upgrades since that would just make everything else take longer given that you'd have to go sell your stuff more often. 

[/list]

[b]General Complaints:[/b]

[list]
[*][i]Spaceship controls:[/i]
Flying in this game is both cool and horribly annoying. Because the game doesn't want you to "crash," it won't let you aim your ship down when you're above the ground by a certain amount, and let me tell you - you're WAAY up in the air at the level in which you're forced to level out. 

Why is this an issue? Because you can't see where you're landing half the time. It becomes a 'guessing' game, and you might end up landing your plane on top of a big mushroom (has happened to me several times) because you're trying to get as close to the POI as you can because walking is SOOO slow. 

But, you get better at getting close the longer you play, which is great, but still. I'd much prefer to stop my ship (yes, it does "hover"), face my ship down, find a spot, and land. But nope, you'll be horizontal to the ground when you get close enough to know what's down there. 

[*][i]Points-of-Interest [POI]:[/i]

The POIs all look generally the same, from one planet to the next. (I haven't been outside of my current galaxy, so if that changes, I don't know - maybe it will? But this was shortsighted on their part. If they can make the animals procedurally generate and all look oddly different, then they could have done the same for the POIs. 

[/list]


Even with all of the huge complaints I have with the game (and trust me, I hate them... they make me want to punch myself in the face everytime I get an achievement or have to interact with a beacon), I still really like the game, and it would be worth buying, but given the lies and deceit, I'd say get it for as cheap as you can.
